beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Boopesh M., and this video is about what changed in the Brutalist toolkit this week. A quick note: this is an AI voice, Kokoro, reading my script. On October twenty-third, Brutalist merged the first three pull requests in its history. And in the same week, it learned to work in 3D.

props.command: What changed in the Brutalist toolkit this week?
output: Oct 23: the first three pull requests ever merged (#1, #3, #4)
thumbnails · setup fixes · SEIS speaker series
plus three new Blender skills: Brutalist goes 3D

beats.role_note: BLUF -- hesitant writer corrects the misconception
beats.narration_text: Here's the whole week in one line. Brutalist isn't just one person's toolkit anymore. Fellows are shipping code into it, and the toolkit just reached a new medium.

contextItems.label: Fellows
contextItems.detail: three pull requests merged on Oct 23

beats.role_note: the week as it happened, from git history
beats.narration_text: Here's the week, straight from the commit history. October eighteenth, two Blender skills land. October twenty-first, a third. Then on the twenty-third, pull requests one, three and four are merged, all within ten seconds.

beats.role_note: real evidence: native-4K thumbnails generated by the PR's own tool
beats.narration_text: Pull request one, from Gaurav, is a thumbnail generator. HTML templates, rendered to YouTube-sized images in the toolkit's own colours, with no faces. The Claude Skills series is locked to one template, so each new video changes only its command. Everything on screen is real output from the repo.

beats.role_note: setup fixes as a checklist that ticks
beats.narration_text: Pull request three, from GitHub user meenu viji, makes a fresh install actually work. Eleven commits. Setup now requires Python three point ten or newer, live-tests caption decoding, caps a library version that was crashing transcription, and the fellows skill now matches a report's loudness to the narration.

beats.role_note: the speaker-series pipeline as a filmstrip
beats.narration_text: Pull request four, from Aditi, handles the longest videos we make. It turns a one to four hour Teams recording of a guest speaker into a finished film: logo reveal, speaker card, then the talk and Q and A, uncut, with word-level mutes for profanity.

And then, 3D. Building walkthrough measures a camera route through a model before a single frame renders. Blender build teaches how you could build a similar model from its finished images. And Blender model build writes the film from the real build evidence, keeping what the AI script did apart from what a person would do by hand.
So here's the takeaway. You don't have to be the maintainer to improve the tool you use. Each of these changes began on a fellow's own branch, and reached everyone through a pull request.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF -- prompt read aloud and discussed
beats.narration_text: Your turn. With the Brutalist repo open, paste this into Claude. Find one thing that slowed me down during setup, and draft a small pull request that fixes it, with a test and a short description. A good answer is small enough to review in five minutes. Not a rewrite.

props.command: Here's the Brutalist repo I just set up. Find one thing that slowed me down during setup, and draft a small pull request that fixes it: the change, one test, and a short PR description.
